paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: David tells God, "apart from You I have no good thing" (Psalm 16:2). Then he says, "The LORD is my chosen portion and my cup; You have made my lot secure" (Psalm 16:5). That's David picking God like it's the first pick off a fresh tray. Nothing else on the tray can fill you up the way He does.

And look at what happens when you pick Him. David says, "I have set the LORD always before me. Because He is at my right hand, I will not be shaken" (Psalm 16:8). Then his heart is glad, and his body "will dwell securely" (Psalm 16:9). Compare that to the people chasing other gods, whose sorrows multiply (Psalm 16:4). I'm telling you, only one of those paths ends with a glad heart.

Then David looks past tonight and past this life. He says, "You have made known to me the path of life; You will fill me with joy in Your presence, with eternal pleasures at Your right hand" (Psalm 16:11). Peter, one of Jesus' apostles, says David was speaking about the resurrection of the Christ (Acts 2:31), and that's why this joy is secure. So hold on to God today, baker, because He holds on to you and He's leading you to the path of life.
